title: @libs/realtime — Developer Implementation Brief
subject: realtime
summary: **Shared real-time transport engine for server→client push.**

purpose.intro: **Shared real-time transport engine for server→client push.**

claims.text: Modules never know or care how events are delivered. They call `push()` on the server and `useRealtimeChannel()` on the client. The transport is an implementation detail hidden inside this library.

If we ever need bidirectional streaming (e.g., collaborative editing), we swap the transport inside `@libs/realtime` — the `push()` function, the `useRealtimeChannel()` hook, and every module that uses them remain unchanged.

reference.statement: This library is named `realtime` because it is **transport-agnostic by design**. The current implementation uses SSE (Server-Sent Events), but the API contract is designed so that switching to WebSockets, long-polling, or any future transport requires **zero changes** in consuming code — modules and apps.

claims.text: No module opens its own connection. No module manages reconnection. No module knows about SSE.

reference.statement: **One connection per user. Modules subscribe to channels. The library handles the rest.**

reference.statement: Manages active SSE connections per user. When a user connects to the stream endpoint, their writable stream is registered. When `push()` is called, the manager writes to all active streams for that user (supports multiple tabs/devices).

reference.statement: The library should also export a factory to create the SSE endpoint (Hono route), so the app just mounts it:

snippets.code:
import type { ConnectionManager } from "./connection-manager";

/**
 * Creates a Hono route handler for the SSE stream endpoint.
 * The app mounts this at its chosen path (e.g., /api/realtime/stream).
 *
 * - Requires authenticated user (app applies auth middleware before this)
 * - Registers the connection in the manager
 * - Keeps the stream open until client disconnects
 * - Cleans up on disconnect
 *
 * Uses Hono's built-in streamSSE helper from "hono/streaming".
 */
export function createStreamRoute(manager: ConnectionManager): HonoHandler;

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Concern | SSE | WebSocket |
|---------|-----|-----------|
| Direction needed | Server→client (notifications, updates) | Bidirectional |
| Reconnection | Built into browser `EventSource` API | Manual implementation |
| Hono support | Native `streamSSE` helper, universal | Needs `@hono/node-ws`, platform-specific |
| Auth | Cookies/headers work normally | Auth is tricky (no custom headers on handshake) |
| Proxies/LBs | Standard HTTP, no upgrade needed | Needs special proxy config |

reference.statement: Client→server actions (mark as read, send message, etc.) are regular HTTP requests. The "real-time" part is always server→client push. SSE covers this perfectly.

claims.text: For multi-process scaling, two options — both hidden inside the library:
**PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY** — Use `pg_notify` when pushing. Each process listens and forwards to its local connections. No new infrastructure.
**Redis pub/sub** — Standard pattern for horizontally scaled real-time. Requires adding Redis.
In both cases, the `push()` and `useRealtimeChannel()` APIs remain identical. The scaling strategy is an internal implementation detail of `@libs/realtime`.

reference.statement: The current `ConnectionManager` is in-memory (Map of userId → streams). This works for single-process deployments, which is what the seed targets.
